object_entity.notes: Malabar coast of southwest India; traditional site of the Thomas Christians; Pantaenus reportedly found Christians using Matthew's Gospel here (Eusebius HE 5.10).

passage.notes: Eusebius on Pantaenus finding Christians in India with a Hebrew Matthew from Bartholomew.

passage.excerpt: A man named Pantaenus was put in charge of the catechetical school at Alexandria, a school whose existence is attested from ancient times. This man had been trained in the Stoic system of philosophy; tradition reports he went as far as India to preach Christ to the Brahmans. Clement of Alexandria names him in his own writings as his instructor, showing that Pantaenus stood in the succession of teachers at Alexandria.

subject_entity.notes: Synod convened c. 244 at Bostra in Arabia to address the monarchian views of Bishop Beryllus who denied Christ's pre-existent divinity; Origen was invited to debate Beryllus and successfully persuaded him to return to orthodox teaching per Eusebius HE 6.33.

object_entity.notes: Capital of the Roman province of Arabia; seat of Bishop Beryllus; site of the synod c. 244 where Origen corrected Beryllus's monarchian views.

evidence.notes: Eusebius locates the synod at Bostra.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: Origen's fame spread throughout the whole world; Beryllus of Bostra, Alexander of Jerusalem, and many other bishops invited him to teach and dispute with heretics; in Caesarea he was ordained presbyter by the bishops of Palestine, which provoked the jealousy of Demetrius of Alexandria.
passage.notes: Eusebius on Origen's fame, ordination controversy, and network of episcopal supporters

subject_entity.notes: Emperor Constantius II sends bishop Theophilus the Indian c. 354 on a diplomatic-missionary embassy to Himyar (South Arabia); Theophilus builds churches in Zafar and Aden per Philostorgius HE 3.4–6.

object_entity.notes: Capital of the Himyarite Kingdom in South Arabia; Theophilus the Indian built a church here c. 354 per Philostorgius HE 3.4.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: Theophilus called the Indian was sent by Emperor Constantius on an embassy to the Himyarites in south Arabia. He was originally from the island of Dibus (Socotra). He converted the Himyarites and built three churches: one in Zafar the capital, one in Aden, and one near the Persian Gulf. He also visited the Aksumites and corrected their worship.
passage.notes: Key source for Arabian/Himyarite Christianity and Theophilus's mission; preserved in Photius's epitome.
